collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder and a child aged 6-13)

collection.description: At a child's naming day, an elder tells how their people came across the sea with nothing: tell it as always, or take questions.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: It's (friend)'s naming day, and (subject), the oldest person at the fire, is asked to tell the family story, the one that's told at every naming. It goes like this: long ago, some of the people of this village came across the sea in canoes, with almost nothing, from a place they could never go back to. Nobody remembers why they had to leave. Only that they did, and that Isola let them stay.

choices.label: Tell It the Way It's Always Told

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) has questions. Why couldn't they go back? (subject) doesn't know. Were they scared? Probably. Were they sad? Yes, for a long time. Are we still sad? (subject) thinks. "Some of us carry a bit of it. You don't have to. But it's yours to know." (friend) thinks about this. Then (friend.he/she) asks if there's cake. There is. That's alright too.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) tells it plainly: the long crossing, the hunger, the first sight of the island, the people already here who shared their fish. (subject.He/she) doesn't say what they left. Nobody ever does. At the end, (subject.he/she) puts a pinch of sand from the beach in (friend)'s hand. "This is where we're from now," (subject.he/she) says. (friend) holds the sand very tightly. It's a solemn moment, and a happy one.
